legend: You are responsible for installing a gas pipeline along a road. Let's consider the road (for simplicity) as a segment [0,n]%%ZSMJ0%% on OX%%ZSMJ1%% axis. The road can have several crossroads, but for simplicity, we'll denote each crossroad as an interval (x,x+1)%%ZSMJ2%% with integer x%%ZSMJ3%%. So we can represent the road as a binary string consisting of n%%ZSMJ4%% characters, where character 0 means that current interval doesn't contain a crossroad, and 1 means that there is a crossroad.

Usually, we can install the pipeline along the road on height of 1%%ZSMJ5%% unit with supporting pillars in each integer point (so, if we are responsible for [0,n]%%ZSMJ6%% road, we must install n+1%%ZSMJ7%% pillars). But on crossroads we should lift the pipeline up to the height 2%%ZSMJ8%%, so the pipeline won't obstruct the way for cars.

We can do so inserting several zig-zag-like lines. Each zig-zag can be represented as a segment [x,x+1]%%ZSMJ9%% with integer x%%ZSMJ10%% consisting of three parts: 0.5%%ZSMJ11%% units of horizontal pipe + 1%%ZSMJ12%% unit of vertical pipe + 0.5%%ZSMJ13%% of horizontal. Note that if pipeline is currently on height 2%%ZSMJ14%%, the pillars that support it should also have length equal to 2%%ZSMJ15%% units.

Each unit of gas pipeline costs us a%%ZSMJ16%% bourles, and each unit of pillar — b%%ZSMJ17%% bourles. So, it's not always optimal to make the whole pipeline on the height 2%%ZSMJ18%%. Find the shape of the pipeline with minimum possible cost and calculate that cost.
Note that you must start and finish the pipeline on height 1%%ZSMJ19%% and, also, it's guaranteed that the first and last characters of the input string are equal to 0.
input: The fist line contains one integer T%%ZSMJ20%% (1≤T≤100%%ZSMJ21%%) — the number of queries. Next 2⋅T%%ZSMJ22%% lines contain independent queries — one query per two lines.

The first line contains three integers n%%ZSMJ23%%, a%%ZSMJ24%%, b%%ZSMJ25%% (2≤n≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ26%%, 1≤a≤108%%ZSMJ27%%, 1≤b≤108%%ZSMJ28%%) — the length of the road, the cost of one unit of the pipeline and the cost of one unit of the pillar, respectively.
The second line contains binary string s%%ZSMJ29%% (|s|=n%%ZSMJ30%%, si∈{0,1}%%ZSMJ31%%, s1=sn=0%%ZSMJ32%%) — the description of the road.
It's guaranteed that the total length of all strings s%%ZSMJ33%% doesn't exceed 2⋅105%%ZSMJ34%%.
output: Print T%%ZSMJ35%% integers — one per query. For each query print the minimum possible cost of the constructed pipeline.
